units.translation: where Pausanias 2, 24, 4 mentions Δία τὸν ἐν θαλάσση [Zeus of the sea] from Aeschylus, so that we do not know which case Aeschylus used.
and one must expect that someone will be lord of Zeus
Ζηνὶ δεσπόσειν τινά [someone will be lord over Zeus]
Δία τὸν ἐν θαλάσση [Zeus of the sea]
he sailed on the breeze of the giant Zephyrus
Thus I corrected for ὀργῆς νοσούσης [of a diseased anger], about which will be said under ὀργή [anger].
words are healers of seething anger
I envy you because you are free from blame
now I envy you for having died before seeing the depth of evils
being enviable, you led a blessed life among the Persians like a god
a penalty is inflicted on a vain tongue
and in eagerness and daring what penalty do you see present?
being enraged by penalties that deprive of money
and having let go -- I will not say the penalty
and do not seek to learn your own toils

In these three places in the books Zwá and ζωῆς [of life] are written in the manuscripts, a form which the tragedians did not use, about which it is said in the Thesaurus vol. 4 p. 55 after Elmsley on Eur. Med. 946.
and in the earth stained with murder life is mingled
for bitter are the vapors and not of life
death is easier than a wretched life
under the darkness of the earth

Triclinius interpolated πραθέντα τλῆναι καὶ ζυγῶν θιγεῖν βία [having been sold to endure and to touch the yoke by force] for π. τλήναι δουλίας μάζης βία [to endure the barley-cake of slavery by force], where Enger rightly has δουλίας μάζης τυχεῖν [to obtain the barley-cake of slavery].
and I first yoked beasts in yokes
he breaks the middle of the yoke
yielding to this necessity, make new the yoke
and your entire yoke of the balance
never to hold the city of Cadmus with slavish yokes
to keep away the slavish yoke from this city
this city has escaped the slavish yoke
to cast a slavish yoke upon Hellas
having cast a yoke upon the neck of the sea
the yoke of strength was loosed
for no one willingly uses a slavish yoke
for one must bear the slavish yoke
when those in power are at the yoke of the spear
πραθέντα τλῆναι καὶ ζυγῶν θιγεῖν βία [having been sold to endure and to touch the yoke by force]
π. τλήναι δουλίας μάζης βία [to endure the barley-cake of slavery by force]
δουλίας μάζης τυχεῖν [to obtain the barley-cake of slavery]
δαμάσω [I will subdue], κλείσω [I will shut], καθέξω [I will hold]. Aeschylus in Circe the satyr-play (fr. 113).
δαμάσω [I will subdue], κλείσω [I will shut], καθέξω [I will hold]. Aeschylus in Circe the satyr-play
from whom she carried the weight of children under her girdle
for how did she nourish you within her girdle, O murderer?
I have cords and girdles, fastenings of robes
but the fame of the dead is alive
